PROJECT 04 / HUMAN–COMPUTER INTERACTION

GESTURECONTROL

A touchless input system that interprets hand landmarks and maps recognized gestures to useful computer actions.

ROLECOMPUTER VISION
YEAR2026

VIEW SOURCE ↗
[ THE PROBLEM ]

MAKE MOVEMENT AN INPUT LANGUAGE.

Conventional controls require physical contact. Gesture Control explores a more natural interface where the camera observes a hand, understands its pose, and triggers a mapped action.

The engineering challenge is not only detecting a hand—it is turning noisy landmark motion into stable, intentional commands.

[ HOW IT WORKS ]

CAMERA TO ACTION.

01 / CAPTURE

READ FRAMES

OpenCV supplies a continuous stream from the webcam.

02 / TRACK

FIND LANDMARKS

MediaPipe identifies key points across the hand and fingers.

03 / INTERPRET

CLASSIFY POSE

Geometric relationships determine which gesture is being shown.

04 / CONTROL

MAP THE ACTION

The recognized gesture triggers the configured media or system command.

[ SYSTEM ]

WHAT IS USED.

LANGUAGE

PYTHON

Gesture logic, event mapping, and application control.

TRACKING

MEDIAPIPE

Fast hand detection and 21-point landmark estimation.

VIDEO

OPENCV

Frame capture, preprocessing, visualization, and feedback.

[ ENGINEERING ]

KEY CONSIDERATIONS.

01

GESTURE STABILITY

Temporal filtering helps avoid accidental actions caused by a single noisy frame.

02

RESPONSIVE FEEDBACK

On-screen landmarks and gesture labels show what the system currently understands.

03

CONFIGURABLE MAPPING

The interpretation layer separates gestures from actions so controls can evolve.
